name: The Roben-sugi of Nigatsu-do
age_estimate: current tree roughly 60 years old, replanted after 1961
access: Free, part of Todai-ji's outer precinct (Nigatsu-do itself has no admission fee)
transport: City loop bus from Kintetsu Nara Station to Daibutsuden Kasuga Taisha-mae, then about 15 min walk uphill
verify_notes: Legend: the infant Roben, later Todai-ji's founding abbot, was said to have been carried off by an eagle and left in the branches of a cedar on this spot; he was found and raised by the monk Jitchu/Gyoshun, and this became the origin story tying Roben to the temple he founded. A stone monument beside the tree records the planting's origin (gururinkansai.com). NOT the original tree: multiple independent sources agree the first Roben-sugi lived roughly 600 years and stood about 21.2m tall, and was destroyed on 16 September 1961 by the Second Muroto Typhoon (max winds 75m/s). Sources disagree on exactly which generation stands today: jinja-tera-gosyuin-meguri.com says a second planting failed to thrive and died, and the present (third) tree was planted 16 March 1967 from a cutting/seed of the second generation; naratrip.com instead describes the present tree as the fourth generation. Neither source gives a reason to doubt the tree standing today is alive and roughly six decades old; the disagreement is only about the count of failed intermediate plantings, not about whether today's tree is genuine. This is a Kyoto Gion-cherry style entry: a young tree on a legendary, signposted spot rather than an ancient specimen itself, and the story should say plainly that it is a replanting after the 1961 storm. Location is shrine-level: sources place it below the slope Nigatsu-do stands on, immediately north of the small Kojo Shrine (興成神社); the coordinate here is a mapped point at that description, not a register or trunk-level source, hence approximate rather than confirmed.
